name: Nanchang
meta_description: TDSC investigative consulting in matters touching Nanchang: supplier and partner due diligence, IP protection and dispute support in Jiangxi's capital.
hero_lede: Investigative consulting for matters that touch Nanchang: due diligence on Jiangxi manufacturers, automotive and electronics suppliers, research supporting intellectual property enforcement before the city's specialised court and arbitration centre, and counterparty checks on state-linked partners. Scoped from Nashville under China's data and security rules.
intro: Nanchang is the capital of Jiangxi province and its largest city. It had 6.67 million permanent residents at the end of 2024 and GDP of about 780 billion yuan in 2024, roughly 118,000 yuan per head. The city's industrial base spans automobiles and parts, aviation, electronics and opto-electronics, food, biomedicine and traditional Chinese medicine, new materials and textiles. Jiangling Motors, where Ford assembles the Transit van, is a long-established local manufacturer. Two national-level zones, the Nanchang National High-tech Industrial Development Zone and the Nanchang Economic and Technological Development Zone, host much of the city's manufacturing and foreign investment, and the Ganjiang New District is a state-designated growth area. Changbei International Airport is Jiangxi's main international gateway, and Nanchang Port is the largest on the Gan River.

Organisations commission investigative work connected to Nanchang mainly in connection with supply chains and partnerships. Foreign buyers and investors source automotive components, electronics, opto-electronic products, pharmaceuticals and textiles from Nanchang producers and need assurance about ownership, related parties, licences and litigation history. Joint ventures and technology licences raise questions about local partners, state-owned shareholders and the protection of know-how, especially in aviation-related and electronics manufacturing. Intellectual property infringement, trade secret leakage through former employees and counterfeit or grey-market goods lead to work supporting enforcement before Nanchang's specialised IP court or arbitration. Companies with operations in the city's development zones also commission internal investigations into procurement fraud, kickbacks and conflicts of interest within local subsidiaries.

matters.title: Automotive and electronics supplier checks
matters.text: Due diligence on Nanchang component makers and electronics and opto-electronics producers before sourcing or investment, covering registered ownership, related companies, administrative penalties, litigation, export history and media, so buyers can judge capacity, integrity and concentration of risk in Jiangxi supply chains.

matters.title: Joint venture partner research
matters.text: Background research on prospective Jiangxi partners and their shareholders, including state-owned and local government investment vehicles, mapping related parties, prior disputes and political and regulatory sensitivities before joint ventures, technology licences or equity investments in Nanchang's development zones.

matters.title: IP infringement and trade secret support
matters.text: Lawful research identifying manufacturers, distributors and online sellers connected to infringing or counterfeit goods, and fact development where former employees may have taken know-how to Nanchang competitors, documented to support action by Chinese counsel before the specialised IP court or arbitration.

matters.title: Internal investigations in subsidiaries
matters.text: Support to counsel and compliance teams investigating procurement fraud, kickbacks, conflicts of interest and undisclosed related-party suppliers within Nanchang subsidiaries, combining analysis of company data provided by the client with registration records of suppliers and employees' outside business interests.

matters.title: Pharmaceutical and TCM partner checks
matters.text: Research into biomedicine and traditional Chinese medicine companies in and around Nanchang, covering ownership, product registrations where public, regulatory penalties, litigation and reputational issues, to support licensing, distribution and acquisition decisions involving Jiangxi's healthcare manufacturers.

local_context.title: Courts and the Nanchang IP court
local_context.text: As provincial capital, Nanchang hosts Jiangxi's provincial judicial institutions, and commercial disputes involving local companies are heard by the people's courts at basic and intermediate level in the city. In July 2018 a specialised Nanchang Intellectual Property Court was established, Jiangxi's first, hearing first-instance civil and administrative cases on patents, technical secrets and new plant varieties across the province. Published judgments are an important lawful research source.

local_context.title: Nanchang Arbitration Commission
local_context.text: Commercial arbitration in the city is administered by the Nanchang Arbitration Commission. In 2016 it opened an intellectual property arbitration centre, described at the time as the fifth of its kind in China and the first in central China, handling patent, trademark, copyright, trade secret and unfair competition disputes. Contracts with Jiangxi parties sometimes name the commission, and its rules and current practice should be checked with counsel.

local_context.title: Development and bonded zones
local_context.text: Nanchang's national high-tech zone, the only national-level high-tech zone in Jiangxi, and its economic and technological development zone hold much of the city's foreign-invested manufacturing. The Nanchang Comprehensive Bonded Zone, formed in 2016 from the former export processing zone, covers about two square kilometres in the high-tech zone and Ganjiang New District, focusing on electronics, biomedicine and bonded logistics. Zone administrations publish investment and enforcement notices.

local_context.title: Registration and local records
local_context.text: Company information for Nanchang businesses is held in China's national enterprise credit information system, maintained through local market regulation bureaus, and shows registered capital, shareholders, legal representatives, administrative penalties and abnormal operation listings. Records of court enforcement, dishonest judgment debtors and published judgments complement registry data. Access to non-public files and personal information is restricted and must go through proper legal channels.

tdsc_approach: For matters touching Nanchang, TDSC begins with a compliance review alongside the client and its counsel: whether the work involves personal information, important data, state-owned shareholders or sensitive technologies such as aviation-related manufacturing. TDSC declines requests that would require covert surveillance, purchased personal records or access to restricted government data. Research relies on enterprise registration data, published judgments and enforcement records, development zone announcements, listing disclosures and Chinese-language trade media. Where a site visit to a Nanchang factory or office is lawful and necessary, TDSC coordinates qualified professionals within a written scope and routes formal evidence collection through Chinese counsel. TDSC has no office in Nanchang.

faqs.q: Can TDSC verify a Nanchang supplier before we place orders?
faqs.a: Yes. TDSC reviews the supplier's registered ownership, related companies, licences where public, administrative penalties, court and enforcement records and media coverage, and can arrange a lawful site visit through qualified local professionals where justified. Findings help assess whether the supplier is real, capable and free of obvious integrity problems.

faqs.q: Can TDSC support an IP case before the Nanchang Intellectual Property Court?
faqs.a: Yes, as a consultant to the client and its Chinese counsel. TDSC researches infringing manufacturers and sellers, their corporate networks and assets from lawful sources. Evidence intended for court, such as notarised test purchases, is collected through counsel and notaries so that it meets Chinese procedural requirements.

faqs.q: Does TDSC research state-owned partners in Jiangxi?
faqs.a: TDSC maps the shareholders, related entities, litigation and published regulatory history of state-owned and local government-linked companies from registration data, disclosures and media. It does not seek internal government information or approach officials. Work involving sensitive sectors is reviewed with counsel before it begins.

faqs.q: How does TDSC handle personal data in Nanchang matters?
faqs.a: TDSC limits collection to what the agreed purpose requires, applies China's Personal Information Protection Law with counsel's guidance, and avoids transferring personal information out of China unless a lawful mechanism applies. Where possible, analysis relies on corporate rather than personal information, and sensitive findings are reported in summary form.

faqs.q: Does TDSC have staff in Nanchang?
faqs.a: No. TDSC has no office, staff or address in Nanchang or elsewhere in mainland China. Engagements are scoped and managed from Nashville. Where lawful local inquiries are needed, TDSC coordinates independent qualified professionals and works with the client's Chinese counsel under a written scope that reflects China's data and security rules.
